messages.subject: Field note: trait ratios across generations
messages.body: In a small working population, observing both purple-stem and green-stem offspring across generations lets you compare real trait counts against your earlier family-tree prediction.

messages.subject: Next observation and the rover checklist
messages.body: Now that we have recorded what actually grew and what observation we should make next, bring that discipline to the garage. The rover checklist is open on the dock board.

messages.subject: What observation comes next
messages.body: Rafi asked the right question: not whether our May prediction looks clever, but what observation we should make next. See you at the rover checklist in the garage.

messages.subject: Two in the field, two at home
messages.body: The garage hatch closes on two in the field and two at home. Every call has a voice at both ends. Check the slope overlay on the ridge map before we roll.

messages.subject: Home watch standing by
messages.body: Hatch sealed: two field seats in the rover, two home voices at the Aurora console. We have your telemetry and return reserve on the big board.

messages.subject: Where the ridge bends out of sight
messages.body: The graded road keeps the slope within limits, but ahead the ridge bends out of sight of our roof antenna. Our radio plan must bend with it—place the relay beacons before the corner.

messages.subject: Line of sight on the Moon
messages.body: Radio waves travel in straight lines and the ridge does not. Good thing we packed three beacons so the link can turn the corner before we do.

messages.subject: Earth desk: ridge route telemetry
messages.body: Aurora, Earth desk. We see the rover on the surveyed contour road and home watch on the console. Keep an unbroken line-of-sight chain all the way to the shadow boundary.

messages.subject: An unbroken chain home on the map
messages.body: Beacons B1, B2 and B3 lock in an unbroken chain home on the map. Before you touch the bright frost patch in the shadow, take a dry regolith reference reading first.

messages.subject: All three hops green
messages.body: Home console confirms an unbroken chain across all three ridge segments. Calibrate the spectrometer on dry ground before measuring the cold-trap patches.

messages.subject: Why a dry reference comes first
messages.body: In a permanently shadowed cold trap, visual brightness alone cannot prove water ice. Recording a dry reference and keeping a negative control lets you verify which samples cross the detection threshold.

messages.subject: Next sealed sample on the shelf
messages.body: Dry reference, two positive ice-bearing samples, and one negative control are logged on the map. Move to the next sealed sample site on the inner shelf—the lamp beam just caught something with corners.

messages.subject: Three sealed tubes
messages.body: Clean work keeping the negative control alongside the two positives. Check the next sealed sample marker on the shelf ahead.

messages.subject: Carrier tethered beside the vault
messages.body: The recovery carrier is tethered beside the vault on the cold-trap shelf. Do not force the latch in the dark—check the thermal probe and seal state before we touch the case.

messages.subject: Straight edges in the shadow
messages.body: Moon rocks do not have ninety-degree corners or serial plates. I tethered the carrier right beside the vault housing so nothing slides on the regolith.

messages.subject: Probe, sleeve, cradle
messages.body: Opening the vault in vacuum would shock whatever is inside. Follow the three recovery steps in order—probe, sleeve, cradle—and bring the whole sealed box home to the dry glovebox.

messages.subject: Cold-mass reading stable
messages.body: Thermal probe logged. Wrap the insulating sleeve and lock the case into the rover cradle before the suit heaters spend any more margin.

messages.subject: Correct call leaving the lid sealed
messages.body: Good restraint at the cold-trap shelf. A field recovery brings the container home intact; it does not open a cold-soaked archive in the dust.

messages.subject: The case is travelling home
messages.body: Log the status exactly as agreed: the case is travelling home, not that the mystery has been solved. Keep the beacon chain live and bring both people and the cradle back to the garage dock.

messages.subject: Cargo mount locked
messages.body: Cradle latched on the rover mount. Remember Amara's wording on the radio: the case is travelling home, not that the mystery has been solved.

messages.subject: Dry glovebox ready after controlled warming
messages.body: Everyone is back inside and the overnight controlled warming curve finished without condensation. My hand is steady near the lid—meet me at the dry glovebox to open the case properly.

messages.subject: Warming curve complete
messages.body: Twelve hours of slow warming and not a drop of frost on the inner seal. Mei has her hand near the lid in the dry glovebox.

messages.subject: Vault inventory: twelve cryo-wells
messages.body: Cold-trap vault case contains twelve numbered sample wells (eleven brassica seed vials and one long-staple cotton vial) plus a handwritten line inside the inner lid.

messages.subject: A line of handwriting under the lid
messages.body: Twelve intact wells logged in the vault ledger, and a line of handwriting under the lid in the same hand as our April seed packet. Bring the photograph to the Earth console window.

messages.subject: Twelve wells and the lid inscription
messages.body: All twelve vials stay sealed in the vault12 inventory. We photographed the handwriting under the lid so we can put the exact evidence to Commander Ferreira during the contact window.

messages.subject: Keep the inscription and the question open
messages.body: You showed me the record cleanly. Keep the saved inscription and its open question on the board. I am booked on the December relief flight; we will finish reading the 2034 files at the same table.

messages.subject: She is coming here
messages.body: Ferreira did not dodge the handwriting under the lid. She asked us to keep the saved inscription and its open question until she lands in December.

messages.subject: Earth desk: twelve-specimen report receipt
messages.body: Aurora, Earth desk. We have your twelve-specimen cold-trap report and the dry reference curves. December transfer manifest is confirmed: one passenger inbound to Shackleton.

messages.subject: The fifth mug and the 8 to 12 December flight
messages.body: Departure notice is up for the 8 to 12 December flight. The fifth locker is labelled, the fifth mug is ready by the rack, and the landing camera goes live on the 12th.

messages.subject: I did not polish the mug
messages.body: Whatever Rafi says, I only wiped dust off the fifth mug once in November. The 8 to 12 December flight lands tomorrow morning—meet at the garage dock camera.

messages.subject: Earth desk: relief lander on final approach
messages.body: Aurora, Earth desk. The 8 to 12 December flight is on final descent to your pad. Commander Ferreira is aboard with your December cargo manifest.
